assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has reshaped measurement and understanding of intergenerational mobility with substantial policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman form a coherent central group for the empirical mobility agenda, though the wider literature has important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base, methods and influence have accumulated over more than a decade.
uncertainties: The candidate description aggregates several linked contributions rather than one sharply bounded discovery.
Interpretation of place-based mobility estimates remains an active research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion fundamentally broadened economic models of behavior and generated a large experimental literature.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt have distinct and complementary central roles in the experimental and theoretical development.
assessment.maturity: The core findings have been repeatedly studied across laboratory, field and applied settings.
uncertainties: The breadth and context dependence of social preferences complicate a single canonical formulation.
Attribution necessarily excludes other foundational experimental researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioral game theory created durable methods and evidence for studying strategic behavior beyond the standard rational benchmark.
assessment.attribution: Plott's market experiments, Camerer's behavioral synthesis and Crawford's strategic-reasoning work provide a defensible three-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: These contributions have influenced theory, experimental practice and applications for decades.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery combines several broad strands with numerous deserving contributors.
External validity of particular laboratory game results remains context-sensitive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on tasks, trade shocks and changing labor demand gave persuasive empirical structure to central explanations for wage and employment polarization.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are closely identified with the linked task and trade-shock evidence.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively tested, extended and incorporated into policy debate.
uncertainties: The relative quantitative importance of technology, trade and institutions varies across settings.
The candidate groups partially distinct research programs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made transparent inference possible when economic assumptions do not justify point identification, improving credibility across empirical economics.
assessment.attribution: Manski is foundational, with Tamer and Molinari central to major econometric developments and applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and has a deep theoretical and applied record.
uncertainties: Its broad methodological lineage makes exact three-person attribution difficult.
Practical uptake remains more uneven than for conventional point-estimation methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression supplied an influential framework for studying distributional relationships concealed by conditional means.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett originated the core method; Chernozhukov represents important modern high-dimensional and distributional extensions.
assessment.maturity: The method is long established and broadly used in economics and adjacent fields.
uncertainties: The foundational contribution is especially concentrated in Koenker and Bassett, while later extensions are diverse.
The proposed grouping spans generations of methodological work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies produced unusually clear evidence on labor-market discrimination and strengthened experimental approaches to discrimination research.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are the most directly attributable pair for the signature correspondence-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated, refined and widely used in economics and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Audit evidence identifies differential treatment within particular application settings, not all mechanisms behind labor-market inequality.
The approach has a longer intellectual history than the selected contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework offered a powerful quantitative account of how distorted factor allocation can generate large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the influential empirical-quantitative framework, with Restuccia a key contributor to its development.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a sustained literature across countries, sectors and policy questions.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect forces other than economically meaningful distortions.
Estimated aggregate gains are sensitive to modeling and measurement assumptions.
